note: What an Electronics Bench puts together (D-158). A design names its parts, what it makes and the Technician skill it needs (none for the toolkit and the computer, so anybody can start). Every part has a reliable source: electronic scrap and circuit boards on the Blackwater exchange, scrap from Kessler Salvage's heaps and office furniture, iron and copper from the quarries and shelves, glass from sand.

designs.title: Circuit boards
designs.note: Two boards from scrap: cheaper than the exchange's, and a repair of a well-off building needs one.

designs.title: Technician's toolkit
designs.note: Opens a utility panel to repair a fault. Forty repairs.

designs.title: Personal computer
designs.note: A desktop for a home or a workshop: the service board and these designs.

designs.title: Diagnostic scanner
designs.note: Carried during a repair, it shows which half of the circuit has the fault.

designs.title: Security array
designs.note: Fitted at a utility panel for an install job: the building's alarm is armed and watched.
